correctness.rationale: Finite Fourier decomposition is exact for arbitrary p,q. For each positive normalized-residue fiber, frame eigenvalues within 1±delta bound its sum Q and zeroth-mode square Z². Positivity yields off-largest mass <=7delta/6, max height error <5delta/8 and squared fiber distance <=1009delta²/576<16delta²/9, giving the claimed 4delta/3 globally. Exact equality and p=2 sharp linear-order witness follow algebraically. CHECK.py independently verified 576 finite numerical assertions, not a proof for all dimensions.

value.rationale: Near-Parseval critical Gabor frames are useful stable synthesis systems. The theorem rigidly identifies all nonnegative exact solutions and proves a dimension-free deterministic inverse stability law from frame-operator error to window sparsity, with a matching linear exponent; this distinguishes robust positive constructions from arbitrary complex flat-Fourier windows and supplies a practical natural structural invariant.
